fields.why: The claims rest on case-control exposure proportions and ORs; the one median hospital stay (13 days) is an incidental descriptive figure. B's 'continuous' can be defended but does not reflect what the claims rest on.

Cases came from German city and district surveillance systems. The brief's 'WHO and other international data: international surveillance' points to A, while 'state or local surveillance' literally fits B; a rule such as 'any non-US surveillance, national or subnational, is international surveillance' would decide it.

agreed_errors.verdict: drop 'stratified analysis by smoked sausage consumption' (class other) as a procedure
agreed_errors.why: Restricting to sausage eaters is a stratification or restriction step that analytic_depth 'stratified/adjusted' already captures. No model or pooled estimator (e.g. Mantel-Haenszel) is named, and the ORs and p-values within the stratum come from the same unnamed test.

brief_issues: The brief should say how non-US subnational surveillance is classed, and whether a plain restriction or stratified re-analysis with no named estimator counts as a procedure.
